simple.meaning: אֶרֶג (ʼereg) is a Hebrew word meaning “a weaving ; a braid ; also a shuttle.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אֶרֶג (H708) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Judges 16:14, with occurrences in Judges, Job.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֶרֶג (H708) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אֶרֶג (H708) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אֶרֶג (ʼereg) / H708 is traced through Judges 16:14, Job 7:6 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a weaving ; a braid ; also a shuttle
definitions.full: H708. ereg אֶ֫רֶג noun [masculine] loom (see GFM POS Oct.1889 ) — אֶרֶג Judg 16:4 hand-loom to which Samson's hair was fastened, plucked up by him ( ׳א object of וַיִּסַּע ; strike out הַיְתַד as gloss, compare GFM above); Job 7:6 אָ֑רֶג מִנִּי קַלּוּ יָמַי my days are swifter than a loom. אַרְגֹּב see רגב . אַרְגָּז see רגז .
